tools.name: ofac_wallet_screen
tools.description: Screens a crypto wallet address (EVM, BTC, TRON, SOL, XMR and every other chain OFAC lists) against all Digital Currency Addresses on the US Treasury OFAC SDN list. Returns sanctioned true/false, verdict block/no_match, SDN entity name, sdnType, programs and the list publish date. Use when an agent

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Resolves live DNS records for any domain or hostname via 1.1.1.1: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA and CAA in one call (type=ALL), or a single type incl. SRV, PTR, DS, DNSKEY, HTTPS. Clean JSON with TTLs, NXDOMAIN flag and DNSSEC-authenticated bit. A URL or email address is reduced to its host. Use

tools.name: email_auth_check
tools.description: Checks a domain's email authentication: parses SPF (+all, ?all, multiple records, over 10 DNS lookups), DMARC (p, sp, pct, rua), DKIM keys (your selector or 15 common ones) and MX, then returns an A-F grade, 0-100 score and coded issues (spf_missing, dmarc_p_none, ...). Use when an agent must judge

tools.name: whois_domain_age
tools.description: Looks up a domain in its registry's RDAP server (the ICANN successor to WHOIS, found via the IANA bootstrap): registration date, age in days/years, newlyRegistered (<30 days), expiry, last change, registrar name + IANA ID, EPP status, nameservers and DNSSEC. No personal contact data. Use when an age

tools.name: email_mx_verify
tools.description: Checks an email address without sending mail or opening SMTP: syntax, domain exists, MX records (or RFC 5321 A/AAAA fallback), RFC 7505 null MX, MX host resolves, disposable-domain list (~9.9k domains), role account (info@, support@) and free provider. Verdict deliverable_domain, risky, undeliverabl

tools.name: url_unshorten
tools.description: Follows a URL's HTTP redirects hop by hop (max 10, page bodies never read) and returns the final URL, status, the full chain and heuristic safety flags: shortener_used, cross_domain_redirect, https_downgrade, ip_address_host, punycode_host, userinfo_in_url, high_abuse_tld, credential_keyword_after_r

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "email_mx_verify" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Checks an email address without sending mail or opening SMTP: syntax, domain exists, MX records (or RFC 5321 A/AAAA fallback), RFC 7505 null MX, MX host resolve…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: dns_lookup, email_auth_check, email_mx_verify, url_unshorten · Private data: ofac_wallet_screen, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, whois_domain_age, email_mx_verify · Public sink: ofac_wallet_screen, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, email_mx_verify.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: dns_lookup, email_auth_check, email_mx_verify, url_unshorten · Private data: ofac_wallet_screen, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, whois_domain_age, email_mx_verify · Public sink: ofac_wallet_screen, dns_lookup, email_auth_check, email_mx_verify

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
